prf:stable-atom-decidable:
Proof Proof of stable atom decidable.

  1. Compute the normal form T_w \in H_{n(K)}(q) via Gröbner–Shirshov reduction (hecke normal form). This terminates in finite time by the Diamond Lemma.
  2. Compute the confinement level (confinement level) \ell(K, q). Sort the finite set of shadow prices and find the smallest \ell such that T_w \in J^\ell(q).
  3. Construct the LP-dual constraint matrix \mathrm{G}(q) \in R^{N \times N}, where N is the number of primitive operators in J^{\ell(K, q)}(q). This set is finite by confinement-level-exists.
  4. Read off the coefficient vector x(K, q) of T_w in the primitive basis, check that it lies in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^N, and evaluate the N coordinates of \mathrm{G}(q)\,x(K, q). Over a ring with decidable order this is a finite computation.

Each step is decidable. Their composition is decidable. \square

Complexity. The bottleneck is step 1, the normal-form reduction. Step 4 is one matrix-vector product of size N. No integer-programming search is needed, because the vector being tested is fixed by T_w.
def:unstable-atom: Definition Unstable atom (failure of normal-form positivity). An atom-knot K is unstable at q if and only if it fails to satisfy the stable atom condition. That is, the coefficient vector x(K, q) of T_w within the confinement filtration J^{\ell(K, q)}(q) either fails to lie in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^N or violates \mathrm{G}(q)\,x(K, q) \geq 0 in some coordinate.
prose:intro-magic-shells: Unwrapping the integer-linear-programming solution counts across the (Z, N) plane isolates the nuclear magic numbers (2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126), the shell closures explained by the spin–orbit shell model of Goeppert Mayer [mayer1949] and of Haxel, Jensen and Suess, as points of Schur–Weyl self-duality where the active Wedderburn partition coincides with its conjugate (\lambda = \lambda'). This section proves the self-duality criterion, distinguishes the compound-\beta shell calibration from the single-wrap nuclear base, and defines the dimensionless magic-shell coupling \kappa.
rem:ilp-solution-count-unwrap:
Remark ILP solution count determines unwrap depth via confinement level. The number of distinct ILP solutions at a given confinement level dictates the unwrap depth required to uniquely specify an atom-knot's normal form.

Let K be an atom at substrate parameter q with normal form currently expressed at level \ell. Let N_\ell(K, q) be the number of integer solutions x \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^M to the Frobenius positivity ILP \mathrm{G}(q)\, x \geq 0 within the confinement filtration J^\ell(q).

The unwrap depth at level \ell is:

  d_\ell(K, q) = \max\bigl(0, N_\ell(K, q) - 1\bigr).

Interpretation:

  • N_\ell = 0: unstable at level \ell. The atom cannot exist in this shorthand. It must decay or fully unwrap.
  • N_\ell = 1: uniquely determined at level \ell. The shorthand suffices; no unwrap is needed.
  • N_\ell = k \geq 2: (k-1)-fold ambiguous at level \ell. One must unwrap k-1 levels to disambiguate via finer normal form structure.

Connection to confinement levels. Each unwrap step expands a shorthand word at level \ell into its normal form at level \ell - 1. The finer level accesses a larger filtration J^{\ell-1}(q) \supsetneq J^\ell(q). This richer operator basis distinguishes previously tied ILP solutions. When a coarse effective description exhibits multiple solutions, zooming to the next-finer scale resolves the ambiguity via operator content.

Computational benefit. Non-magic atoms typically exhibit N_\ell = 1 at the coarsest useful level. A single inter-nucleon configuration suffices. Magic atoms exhibit N_\ell \geq 2 at the nucleon level. Shell closure permits multiple equivalent assemblies of the closed shell. Each corresponds to a distinct normal form at the quark level. Double-magic atoms exhibit N_\ell \geq 3 because both proton and neutron closures contribute degeneracy.

Formal statement. Let K be an atom-knot. Then:

  \boxed{\; \text{NF-depth}(K, q) = \text{coarsest level } \ell \text{ with } N_\ell(K, q) = 1 \;}

Computing the normal form at exactly this depth fully specifies the atom's categorical structure. Deeper computation is redundant; shallower computation leaves ambiguity.

Example (proton gluon derivation). The proton's 9-crossing element \mathcal{B}_3 \times \Delta_3(\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}) admits N_\ell = 84 feasible ILP solutions at the baryon level. Minimizing |\mathrm{tr}_M| selects the unique \sigma_0 \to \sigma_0 solution. If a tie occurs, the framework demands unwrapping to the quark level, where the ILP separates them.

Computational shortcut. Adaptive unwrap reduces cost: storage and Gröbner reduction scale with n_{\text{strands}}^{\text{used}} rather than uniformly with 3A.
prop:shell-schur-weyl-self-duality:
Proposition Schur-Weyl justification of shell-operator self-duality. Let H_n(R, q) be the Iwahori–Hecke algebra with generators \sigma_i satisfying \sigma_i^2 = h\,\sigma_i + 1, where h = q - q^{-1}. The assignment

  \#\colon \sigma_i \;\longmapsto\; -\sigma_i^{-1} \;=\; h - \sigma_i

extends to an algebra automorphism of H_n(R, q). When H_n(R, q) is split semisimple, \# maps the central primitive idempotent e_\lambda to e_{\lambda^*}, where \lambda^* is the conjugate partition. Under quantum Schur–Weyl duality

  V^{\otimes n}
  \;=\;
  \bigoplus_{\lambda\,\vdash\,n}
    V_{\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{gl}_k)}(\lambda)
    \;\otimes\;
    V_{H_n(R, q)}(\lambda),

this is the Hecke-side form of the transpose \lambda \leftrightarrow \lambda^*.

Consequently, for

  \sigma_{\mathrm{shell}}
  \;=\;
  \sum_{\lambda\,\vdash\, A_{\mathrm{magic}}}
    x_\lambda \cdot e_\lambda
  \;\in\; H_{A_{\mathrm{magic}}}(q),

the shell-operator self-duality constraint

  x_\lambda \;=\; x_{\lambda^*}
  \qquad\text{for all}\quad \lambda \vdash A_{\mathrm{magic}}

holds if and only if \#(\sigma_{\mathrm{shell}}) = \sigma_{\mathrm{shell}}.

The transpose is not representation duality on the quantum-group side: in general V_{\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{gl}_k)}(\lambda^*) \not\cong V_{\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{gl}_k)}(\lambda)^*. For k = 2 and \lambda = (2) the two sides have dimensions 1 and 3.
prf:shell-schur-weyl-self-duality:
Proof Proof of shell schur weyl self duality. 1. \# is well defined. Put \tau_i = h - \sigma_i. From \sigma_i^2 = h\sigma_i + 1,

  \tau_i^2 \;=\; h^2 - 2h\sigma_i + \sigma_i^2 \;=\; h(h - \sigma_i) + 1 \;=\; h\,\tau_i + 1,

so \tau_i satisfies the Hecke quadratic. For adjacent i, j, expanding gives

  \tau_i\tau_j\tau_i - \tau_j\tau_i\tau_j
  \;=\; h^2(\sigma_j - \sigma_i) + h(\sigma_i^2 - \sigma_j^2) - (\sigma_i\sigma_j\sigma_i - \sigma_j\sigma_i\sigma_j),

which vanishes by the quadratic and braid relations. Far commutativity is immediate. Since \tau_i^2 = h\tau_i + 1 again, \# \circ \# = \mathrm{id}, so \# is an automorphism. The identity h - \sigma_i = -\sigma_i^{-1} follows from \sigma_i(\sigma_i - h) = 1.

2. \# transposes the blocks. In the split semisimple case, twisting the Specht module S^\lambda by \# gives the dual Specht module of \lambda^*, which is isomorphic to S^{\lambda^*} (see Mathas, Iwahori–Hecke algebras and Schur algebras, Ch. 3, and [dipper-james1986]). Hence \#(e_\lambda) = e_{\lambda^*}. At q = 1 this is the twist by the sign character, V_\lambda \otimes \mathrm{sgn} \cong V_{\lambda^*}.

3. Fixed points. Applying \#,

  \#(\sigma_{\mathrm{shell}}) \;=\; \sum_\lambda x_\lambda\, e_{\lambda^*} \;=\; \sum_\lambda x_{\lambda^*}\, e_\lambda .

The e_\lambda are linearly independent, so \#(\sigma_{\mathrm{shell}}) = \sigma_{\mathrm{shell}} if and only if x_\lambda = x_{\lambda^*} for every \lambda. \square

Scope. Steps 1 and 3 are proved here. Step 2 is cited.

Relation to existing propositions. Whether \sigma_{\mathrm{shell}} is in fact \#-invariant is not settled here.
rem:shell-schur-weyl-self-duality-interp:
Remark Physical interpretation: shell closures as charge-conjugate-invariant braids. Shell closures in nuclei correspond to charge-conjugate-invariant braid elements in H_{A_{\mathrm{magic}}}(q). This categorical structure enforces three physical constraints:

  • Parity conservation. The nuclear strong interaction conserves parity because shell closures respect charge conjugation.
  • Isospin doubling. Proton-neutron interchange symmetry emerges at closed shells via isospin SU(2) doubling.
  • CP conservation. Shell-level CP violation vanishes because parity-odd channels cancel between \lambda and \lambda^* contributions.

Parity-violating phenomena arise at level 3 (the inter-nucleon pair), where conjugate symmetry breaks via skein asymmetry. At level 4 (the shell) these constraints hold exactly when the shell operator is invariant under the transpose automorphism \#; that invariance is a hypothesis here, not a proved property of \sigma_{\mathrm{shell}}.
prop:compound-beta-shell-calibration:
Proposition Compound β-decay calibration across magic shells. Let E_0^{(2)} = \mathfrak{Q}_\beta be the free-neutron β-decay Q-value, the CAL-2 proxy, kept as a symbol. A β-decay (Z, N) \to (Z+1, N-1) preserves A, so the shell it can cross is a proton or neutron shell: let it cross a magic number, either Z < Z_{\mathrm{magic}} \le Z+1 or N-1 < N_{\mathrm{magic}} \le N, with magic numbers in \{2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126\}. Assume the parent contains \sigma_{\mathrm{shell}} and the daughter contains a different shell operator or a cross-shell transition. Then the Q-value of the magic-crossing decay is:

  \mathfrak{Q}_\beta(\text{magic-crossing})
  \;=\;
  E_0^{(2)} \cdot
  \Bigl(
    \bigl|\mathrm{tr}_M^{\mathrm{parent}}\bigr|
    \;-\;
    \bigl|\mathrm{tr}_M^{\mathrm{daughter}}\bigr|
    \;-\;
    \bigl|\mathrm{tr}_M^{\mathrm{e^- + \bar\nu}}\bigr|
  \Bigr).

Equivalently, the shell-binding target y_{\mathrm{target}}(A_{\mathrm{magic}}) correlates to the cumulative β-decay chain reaching the magic anchor via the categorical trace. To formalize the full binding scale, one combines multiple β-decay Q-values along the isobar chain through the magic anchor.

Scope. The single magic-crossing Q-value identity above rests on the categorical trace. The compound-chain extension — combining Q-values along the isobar chain to isolate a shell-binding target — is exploratory: it subtracts model-predicted non-magic Q-values (a circular step) and carries an unresolved unit mismatch. It is therefore not a fit-free calibration and is not wired into any production shell-binding target.
rem:compound-beta-shell-calibration-key-:
Remark Magic-crossing Q-value measures the difference of shell operators. Non-magic vs magic \beta-decays (key distinction).

For magic-crossing decays, the \mathcal{Q}_q-value measures the strict difference in shell-operator contributions between parent and daughter, never the absolute shell magnitude itself. The parent intrinsically carries \sigma_{\mathrm{shell}}. The daughter realizes a distinct shell operator or a cross-shell transition.

  1. The shell y_{\mathrm{target}} values are never independently calibrated. They follow strictly from \beta-decay \mathcal{Q}_q-values and level-3 shadow prices.
  2. The shell sector introduces no new calibration. One retains E_0 = \mathfrak{Q}_\beta as the pure H^2 input for the three-calibration discipline. Shell binding derives entirely from decay-chain \mathcal{Q}_q-values and level-3 shadow prices.
  3. Predictions for all magic-anchor binding energies are contingent on the empirical \beta-decay Q-value table (the per-isotope measured Q-values). Beyond the single CAL-2 anchor E_0 = \mathfrak{Q}_\beta, that table is experimental input — so these predictions are not parameter-free: the shell sector adds no new substrate calibration, but it consumes the measured \beta-decay chain as data.

Numerically, E_0^{(2)} = \mathfrak{Q}_\beta \approx 0.782 MeV, the measured free-neutron value.

def:magic-shell-coupling-kappa:
Definition The expression \kappa_{\mathrm{closed}} = -E_0 \log(1/h) / [3]_q!. Let q be a substrate parameter and m_e a mass scale. The expression \kappa_{\mathrm{closed}} is

  \kappa_{\mathrm{closed}}(q, m_e)
  \;=\; -\,\frac{E_0 \cdot \log(1/h)}{[2]_q \cdot [3]_q},
  \qquad
  E_0 = \frac{m_e}{q(q-1)}, \quad h = q - q^{-1},

where [n]_q = (q^n - q^{-n}) / (q - q^{-1}) is the balanced q-bracket.
rem:magic-shell-coupling-kappa-remark:
Remark Status and proved properties of \kappa_{\mathrm{closed}}. No physical quantity is claimed for the expression \kappa_{\mathrm{closed}}. At the substrate parameter it evaluates to \kappa_{\mathrm{closed}} \approx -1.0704. It was formerly proposed as the per-excess slope of a magic-shell coupling; that identification is withdrawn, for the reason recorded below. The name is retained because the corpus refers to it, not because the identification stands.

Reason for the withdrawal.

The expression was matched, to 3.4 \times 10^{-4}, against a measured value of \approx -1.0708\;\text{MeV}. That value is the electrostatic energy of {}^{3}He's pp pair, attributed to the proton–neutron interface asymmetry.

The fit that produced it ran at two anchors and disagreed with itself:

anchor excess (n_{pp} - n_{nn}) slope
{}^{3}He (2,1) +1 -1.0707908\;\text{MeV}
{}^{3}H (1,2) -1 +0.2023095\;\text{MeV}

Opposite signs, a factor of 5.3 apart. The hypothesis under test was that a single coefficient holds across the anchors, and the producing computation recorded that it does not. The {}^{3}He arm became the published value; the {}^{3}H arm was not carried forward.

Those two nuclides differ in exactly one respect besides the sign of the excess: {}^{3}He contains a pp pair and {}^{3}H does not. Restoring that electrostatic energy removes the discord. Both residuals become negative — under every radius model tried, including the one derived from \bar\lambda_\pi and two independent alternatives — and under the derived radius they agree to 0.021\;\text{MeV}, essentially the {}^{4}He residual of 0.022\;\text{MeV} measured where the excess vanishes identically.

A term proportional to (n_{pp} - n_{nn}) must change sign between anchors of excess +1 and -1. What survives the correction does not: it is an excess-independent offset of order 0.2\;\text{MeV}, three to fifteen times smaller than the matched value. The excess coefficient is zero.

That single diagnosis accounts for the two independent negatives found before it. No term of this form and size appears in mirror-split binding data at A = 3, 15, 39, because the coefficient vanishes. And the original fit contradicted itself because it was describing an electrostatic energy with a categorical form, and only one of its two anchors has one.

Proved properties of the expression.

The following hold independently of any physical reading, and are unaffected by the withdrawal.

The bracket is the canonical balanced q-integer: [n]_q as written here coincides the library's balanced q-integer, unconditionally and including on the degenerate locus, so this definition introduces no competing q-integer convention.

The denominator is a q-factorial. [2]_q \cdot [3]_q = [3]_q!, hence

  [2]_q \cdot [3]_q \;=\; [3]_q! \;=\; \frac{q^3}{y_{(3)}(q)},

the inverse Markov weight of the trivial partition (3) \vdash 3. This is the reusable content of the block. The index 3 is the strand count of a single nucleon — the nucleon is the Borromean link, carried by the braid word (\sigma_1 \sigma_2^{-1})^3 \in B_3 — and the same normalization appears in the Borromean observable F_{\mathrm{Bor}} = |\mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}})| / y_{(3)}(q).

The sign is forced. For q > 1, m_e > 0, and 0 < h < 1: E_0 > 0, \log(1/h) > 0, and [2]_q, [3]_q > 0, so \kappa_{\mathrm{closed}} < 0. This is a property of the expression and is asserted of nothing else.

A separate question, deliberately not attached here.

After the electrostatic correction, an excess-independent offset of order 0.2\;\text{MeV} remains at A = 3 that the same form does not exhibit at A = 4, where its residual is 0.022\;\text{MeV}. That is a real and unexplained baseline. It is not the quantity this block was about, and giving it this block's name would repeat the error the withdrawal corrects.

Definition Quantum dilogarithm disambiguation: \Phi_q (product form) vs -\mathrm{Li}_2^q(-z) (Kashaev integration limit). Two distinct functions appear in the QOU mass formulae. One must not conflate them:

Name Symbol Closed form Behaviour near z = 1
Quantum dilogarithm product \Phi_q(z) \prod_{k=1}^{\infty} (1 - q^{-k}z)^{-1} Unbounded (\Phi_q(0.989) \approx 6.7 \cdot 10^5 at q_0)
