The historical paper-level identity:

  \Phi_q(z) \;\stackrel{?}{=}\; \int_0^z \frac{\ln_q(1+t)}{t}\,dt
       \;\stackrel{?}{=}\; \prod_{k\geq 1}(1 - q^{-k}z)^{-1}

is false. The integral evaluates to the bounded quantity -\mathrm{Li}_2^q(-z), not the unbounded \Phi_q(z). The two sides differ by six orders of magnitude at z = 0.989.
rem:gluon-stabiliser-ledger:
Remark The gluon ledger: what step 4 enumerates, and why the trefoil loses. Step 4 of the derived atom says the integer LP dual "selects the minimum gluon", and the proton block says it "enumerates all feasible gluon combinations and selects the configuration minimizing |\mathrm{tr}_M|". Neither says what the enumeration ranges over. This remark says it. The answer dissolves the question it was written to settle: nothing is excluded, so no exclusion argument is owed.

The feasible set. The confinement-layer operator selection rule frames the candidate search. The stabiliser K ranges over non-trivial braid words up to a crossing cap; the constraint is positivity of the resulting state on the Temperley--Lieb quotient; the objective is minimum crossing number with |\mathrm{tr}_M(x\cdot K)| as tiebreak. The producer behind the nucleon numbers enumerates words over \{\sigma_0,\sigma_1,L_+,L_-\} of length at most three — 4 + 4^2 + 4^3 = 84 candidates, which is the count the unwrap-depth remark reports for the proton at baryon level. So the range is not "combinations of L_\pm". It is every braid word inside the cap, and the four-letter alphabet composes to all six normal-form basis words, e^- included.

The electron word is inside it. The natural worry is why the stabiliser may not be e^- = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0: it is a basis word exactly as L_\pm are, and like them it has \mathrm{Vol} = 0, so nothing topological separates them. It is not excluded. As a three-letter braid word it sits in the enumeration — reached as \sigma_0\cdot L_-, or as L_+\cdot\sigma_0 — and it is admissible: applied to either bare nucleon it leaves the state Frobenius-positive. It loses, and it loses under either objective the corpus states. On |\mathrm{tr}_M| it is beaten by an order of magnitude or more for both nucleons. On crossing count it costs three, and both nucleons have admissible stabilisers costing one or two. That is a defeat in the minimisation, not a prohibition, and it is the only answer the construction supports.

Nor is double counting. The gluon does redistribute normal-form weight from \sigma_1 into the e^- channel, so e^- is the output of stabilisation. That is a consequence of the selection, not a constraint on the search: an e^- input would be a different, worse candidate, not a quantity counted twice.

Hyperbolic volume decides nothing here. Where a competing channel carries a hyperbolic constituent, volume settles the selection outright — the Borromean rings carry 8G and a torus link carries none. That is what happens one step earlier, at the antiquark disposal. That route is unavailable at step 4. All five non-identity basis words are torus-type with \mathrm{Vol} = 0, so volume separates none of them, and the whole selection falls to \mathrm{tr}_M and crossing count.

Crossing-count open question. Both nucleons carry two gluon crossings rather than a two-versus-four asymmetry. For the neutron braid \mathcal{B}_3(\mathfrak{u},\mathfrak{d},\mathfrak{d}), the eleven-crossing decomposition — six crossings from \mathcal{B}_3, three from the quark triad, and two from the gluon stabiliser — yields \mathrm{net}(\mathfrak{n}) = +0.7976 on the k-ladder (whereas thirteen crossings give 1.2359). The proton construction likewise applies a single L_- = \sigma_1\sigma_0 of two crossings. Because both nucleons share the same gluon-crossing count, the mass splitting \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{n}} - \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{p}} (and hence \mathfrak{Q}_\beta) does not arise from a gluon-crossing difference.

A narrower discrepancy remains between the one-crossing and two-crossing stabiliser readings: under the minimum-crossing objective of confinement-layer operator selection, a single-crossing stabiliser (\sigma_1, crossing count 1) strictly dominates a two-crossing stabiliser (\sigma_0\sigma_0 or L_- = \sigma_1\sigma_0, crossing count 2), so the two counts cannot both arise from the same objective without an additional tie-breaking or parity constraint.

The feasible set itself is well defined and e^- is strictly suboptimal within it; determining which stabiliser the canonical objective selects remains open.
def:categorical-neutron:
Definition Neutron (categorical). The neutron is the baryon characterized by the 1 + 2 crossing partition: one up quark and two down quarks embedded in the Borromean braid \mathcal{B}_3.

  \mathfrak{n} = \mathcal{B}_3(\mathfrak{u},\mathfrak{d},\mathfrak{d})
rem:categorical-neutron-properties:
Remark Neutron: NF construction, mass, transition, and charge. The neutron definition establishes the \mathcal{B}_3(\mathfrak{u},\mathfrak{d},\mathfrak{d}) baryon. One derives its normal form, mass, \beta-decay transition, and Coulomb charge.

Step 1: Borromean braid NF. As in the proton construction, one finds \mathrm{net}(\mathcal{B}_3) = +1.000, establishing intrinsic Hopf link content without an independent \mathcal{L}_H factor.

Step 2: Typed crossings + gluon stabilisation. The two down quarks induce stronger -h_{\mathrm{A}} shifts than the single down quark of the proton.

A single L_- = \sigma_1\sigma_0 is what the construction applies. The integer LP dual selects L_- as the minimum-action stabiliser, for a total of 11 crossings (6 from \mathcal{B}_3, 3 from quarks, 2 from gluons), and \mathrm{net}(\mathfrak{n}) = +0.7976 is the eleven-crossing value (gluon-stabiliser ledger).

Under the Markov trace used here, with \mathrm{tr}_M(e^-) = h z^2 + z from the Markov recursion, the \sigma_0 channel is positive at every step of the typed build: the \mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d} crossing and the corresponding proton element give \mathrm{tr}_M = +0.408 and +0.544. There is no Frobenius-positivity instability, and so no difference of instability depth to carry a neutron–proton mass split.

A crossing-depth mechanism for the neutron–proton mass split is therefore open; the gluon ledger carries the full measurement.

What remains invariant is the scope of the enumeration: every non-trivial braid word inside the crossing cap, the electron word e^- included, is admissible and is excluded only because it does not attain the minimum of the objective.

Step 3: Neutron NF (with gluon). At q_0 \approx 1.1100:

  \mathrm{net}(\mathfrak{n}) = +0.7976

Relative to the proton (\mathrm{net} = +1.0065), the additional down quark demands a larger L_+ compensation (-0.2206 versus -0.1114). After gluon stabilisation, the e^- channel (e^- \approx +1.0) dominates both nucleons.

Transition: proton \to neutron. The normal-form difference yields the dimensionless \beta-decay transition:

  \Delta\mathrm{net}(\mathfrak{n} - \mathfrak{p})
  = 0.7976 - 1.0065 = -0.2089

The uniform energy scale \mathfrak{E}_0 = \mathfrak{Q}_\beta / |\Delta\mathrm{net}| \approx 4.155 MeV converts these coefficient differences directly to MeV.

Mass.

  \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{n}} =
  2\mathcal{S}_{\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}}(q) + \mathcal{S}_{\mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d}}(q)

At the CODATA value q_0, the base mass is \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{n}}(q_0) \approx 939.565\;\text{MeV} MeV, derived strictly from the substrate parameter. The resulting proton--neutron mass splitting is exactly:

  \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{n}} - \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{p}} =
  \mathcal{S}_{\mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d}}(q) - \mathcal{S}_{\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}}(q)
  \approx 1.293 \text{ MeV}

This splitting arises from the Skein resolution asymmetry between the \mathfrak{u}\text{-}\mathfrak{u} and \mathfrak{d}\text{-}\mathfrak{d} crossing pairs within the rigid \mathcal{B}_3 structure.

Coulomb charge.

  Q(\mathfrak{n}) =
  1 \cdot (+\tfrac{2}{3}) + 2 \cdot (-\tfrac{1}{3}) = 0.

The sum vanishes, and the arithmetic is the Standard Model's. What it is not is a consequence of the crossing-orientation mechanism. A single positive-orientation unknot \mathfrak{u} cannot cancel two negative-orientation unknots \mathfrak{d} of equal magnitude. The cancellation above works only because |Q_{\mathfrak{u}}| = 2|Q_{\mathfrak{d}}|, and orientation reversal is a mirror, so it forces the two magnitudes to be equal (down quark). Writing Q(\mathfrak{u}) = a and hence Q(\mathfrak{d}) = -a, the neutron carries a - 2a = -a and the proton 2a - a = +a: the mechanism makes the neutron the proton's exact opposite, and a neutral neutron forces every quark charge to vanish. The quark charges are therefore an adopted input here, not a derived one. The inter-neutron Hopf crossings acquire the q^{-1} coefficient associated with negative crossings.
def:categorical-meson:
Definition Meson (categorical). A meson is a valence-2 hadron: a quark--antiquark pair bound by the Hopf link \mathcal{L}_H. One forms the meson from two independent quark--antiquark productions, pairing a quark from one with an antiquark from the other:

  \mathfrak{M}
  = 
  T_{01} \cdot \mathcal{L}_H \cdot T_{10}

where:

  • T_{01} = \sigma_0\sigma_1 = L_+ is the up-type crossing pair (knot notation); its closure in B_3 is the unknot.
  • T_{10} = \sigma_1\sigma_0 = L_- is the down-type crossing pair.
  • \mathcal{L}_H = \sigma_0\sigma_1 binds the two constituents.

The full braid word is (\sigma_0\sigma_1)^2 \cdot \sigma_1\sigma_0, containing 6 crossings on 3 strands.

Normal form (step-by-step Hecke reduction). One writes h = h_{\mathrm{A}} = q - q^{-1} and applies the Hecke relation \sigma_i^2 = h\sigma_i + \mathbf{1} and the braid relation \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 = \sigma_1\sigma_0\sigma_1.

Step 1. For the bound pair T_{01} \cdot \mathcal{L}_H = (\sigma_0\sigma_1)^2 = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0\sigma_1, one applies the braid relation to the rightmost three generators to yield \sigma_0 \cdot \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 = \sigma_0^2 \cdot L_-. The Hecke relation reduces this to:

  (\sigma_0\sigma_1)^2 = h \cdot e^- + L_-

Step 2. One multiplies by T_{10} = \sigma_1\sigma_0:

Factor Product Hecke reduction
L_- \cdot L_- \sigma_1\sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 braid + Hecke: h \cdot e^- + L_+
e^- \cdot L_- \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 \cdot \sigma_1\sigma_0 two braid + Hecke steps: h^2 e^- + hL_+ + hL_- + \sigma_1

Collecting terms yields the exact normal form:

  \mathfrak{M}_+ =
  \underbrace{h}_{\sigma_1}\sigma_1 + \underbrace{(h^2 + 1)}_{L_+}\sigma_0\sigma_1 + \underbrace{h^2}_{L_-}\sigma_1\sigma_0 + \underbrace{(h^3 + h)}_{e^-}\sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0

At the CODATA root q_0 \approx 1.1100 (h \approx 0.2091):

  \mathrm{NF}(\mathfrak{M}_+) \approx 0.209\,\sigma_1 + 1.044\,L_+ + 0.044\,L_- + 0.218\,e^-

yielding \mathrm{net}(\mathfrak{M}_+) \approx +1.515.

The mirror meson \mathfrak{M}_- = T_{10} \cdot \mathcal{L}_H \cdot T_{01} maintains identical net amplitude but exchanges \sigma_1 for \sigma_0:

  \mathrm{NF}(\mathfrak{M}_-) \approx 0.209\,\sigma_0 + 1.044\,L_+ + 0.044\,L_- + 0.218\,e^-

Both mesons carry identical L_\pm (L_+ + L_-) and e^- content, differing only in the single-generator excitation.

Particle content. The dominant L_+ term (coefficient \approx 1.044) establishes the binding. The e^- component (\approx 0.218) encodes the residual lepton channel. In contrast, the bare quark--antiquark pair (T_{01} \cdot T_{10}) yields \mathrm{net} = +1.418 and contains a neutrino \nu component in place of the Hopf links. The Hopf link binding actively replaces the neutrino channel and increases the net amplitude by \approx 0.097.
prop:meson-scale-independence:
Proposition The meson mass scale m_\pi is independent of (m_\mathfrak{e}, q_0). The pion mass m_\pi cannot be derived from the substrate parameters (m_\mathfrak{e}, q_0) alone. The Hecke algebra determines the relative meson mass spectrum (character ratios between mesons) but not the absolute scale m_\pi.

Archimedean specialisation. The scale statement is evaluated over \mathbb{R} — hyperbolic volumes, the MeV meson scale, and the CAL-3 numerical calibration. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall.
rem:meson-scale-independence-calibration: Remark Calibration structure and the volume-zero geometric core of meson-scale independence.
prf:meson-scale-independence:
Proof Proof of meson scale independence. (Representation-theoretic and topological.)

The baryon mass formula uses \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) / \hbar_q^2 as the geometric normalization. \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) = 8G > 0 is the hyperbolic volume of the Borromean complement. The meson's binding topology is the Hopf link L_+. Its complement is T^2 \times I, a Seifert-fibred space rather than a hyperbolic one, so \mathrm{Vol}(\text{Hopf complement}) = 0. Without a non-zero hyperbolic volume, there is no geometric invariant to set the meson mass scale from (m_\mathfrak{e}, q_0).

The Hecke character ratios under additional crossings are derived: \chi^{(3)}(K)/\chi^{(3)}(\pi) = q^2, \chi^{(2,1)}(K)/\chi^{(2,1)}(\pi) = 1/(h^2+1), \chi^{(1^3)}(K)/\chi^{(1^3)}(\pi) = q^{-2}. These determine m_K/m_\pi (given m_\pi) but not m_\pi itself. \square
rem:pion-mass-hyperbolic-threshold:
Remark Why m_\pi is a calibration: the pion sits below the hyperbolic threshold. The scale-independence proof attributes the missing pion scale to the meson's binding topology: the Hopf link complement is T^2 \times I, Seifert-fibred rather than hyperbolic, so \mathrm{Vol} = 0 and there is no geometric invariant to set m_\pi from (m_\mathfrak{e}, q_0). That is correct, but it reads as a fact about one link. It is a fact about where the pion sits in a ladder, and stating it that way explains the calibration structure rather than merely reporting it.

The ladder. The fundamental knot operator basis assigns the same braid word to three particles at successive powers:

n (\sigma_1\sigma_2^{-1})^n closure type \mathrm{Vol}
1 \sigma_1\sigma_2^{-1} unknot trivial 0
2 figure-eight 4_1 hyperbolic hyperbolic \approx 2.0299
3 Borromean rings L6a4 hyperbolic hyperbolic \approx 7.328 = 8G

The pion is the n = 1 rung: the pion braid is a half figure-eight, \mathfrak{M}_+ sharing its eigenvalue phase on V_{(2,1)} with \sigma_1\sigma_2^{-1}, and 4_1 = (\sigma_1\sigma_2^{-1})^2 is exactly the square of the pion-type rotation.

Hyperbolic volume switches on at n = 2. So the vanishing at the pion is not a property of the Hopf link in particular; every rung below n = 2 is a torus knot or the unknot, and the operator basis states the rule for those directly — torus knots carry zero hyperbolic volume, hyperbolic knots carry positive volume which translates to mass via \mathrm{Vol}(K)/\hbar_q^2. The pion has no volume-derived mass because it lies below the threshold of its own family.

This is what forces the calibration set. The three anchors are CAL-1 = m_\mathfrak{e}, CAL-2 = P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta} (fixing q_0), CAL-3 = m_\pi. The two mass anchors are exactly the two \mathrm{Vol} = 0 particles: the electron is the trefoil \sigma_1^3, a torus knot; the pion is the n=1 rung. Every derived mass is then either hyperbolic — the muon through m_\mu/m_\mathfrak{e} = \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\hbar_q^2, the nucleon through 8G — or a Hecke character ratio off a \mathrm{Vol} = 0 anchor, as m_K/m_\pi is. There are two mass calibrations rather than one or three because the volume formula reaches exactly the hyperbolic sector, and two particles of the catalogue sit outside it.

A correction the table invites. The operator basis describes the \mathrm{Vol} = 0 entries as "the massless, force-carrying sector". That reading is already contradicted inside the same table: the electron sits there with \mathrm{Vol} = 0 and is the mass unit of the whole framework. The defensible statement is weaker and is the one used above — \mathrm{Vol} = 0 means the mass is not derivable from volume, not that it is zero. The neutrino and the force carriers are massless for other reasons; the electron and the pion are not massless at all, they are uncalibrated by this route, which is why they are measured instead.
prose:eightfold-intro:
Introduction.

The previous chapter established the knot-particle dictionary: each observable particle corresponds to a specific braid configuration in the Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_n(q), and the confinement hierarchy organises these configurations into shells. The question this chapter takes up is: why do these particles fall into the octets and decuplets of the Eightfold Way of Gell-Mann and Ne’eman?

The candidate answer lies in the representation theory of three-strand braiding --- but the chapter must open with a warning about the shape of that answer, because the obvious reading of it is wrong.

Two different A_2s. The braid group B_3 and its q-deformation H_3(q) have Coxeter type A_2: the Coxeter quotient of B_3 is W(A_2) \cong S_3, permuting the three strands. This is true, but it is true by construction --- the braid group on n strands has Coxeter type A_{n-1} by definition, so choosing n = 3 is what puts A_2 there. It is not a structural theorem about the substrate, and nothing is derived from it.

The A_2 that the eightfold way needs is a different one: the Lie algebra \mathfrak{sl}_3 of flavour \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}}, which in quantum Schur--Weyl duality [jimbo1986] (the baryon-multiplet section) is the partner acting on the fibre V, and which appears only when \dim V = N = 3. The two A_2s coincide in name --- and in this chapter's diagrams --- solely because n = 3 has been set and N = 3 is wanted. Setting n = 3 does not make N = 3.

This distinction is the chapter's central honesty constraint, and the reason that section records the N = 3 problem as the chapter's principal open problem rather than as a solved step: the single-fibre construction of the braiding chapter yields a quantum form of \mathrm{SU}(2), with \dim V = 2, and no choice of q raises it. Every flavour-\mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}} statement below is therefore conditional on N = 3, and is marked as such.

The root-system section derives the A_2 root system from the Hecke relations of H_3(q) and identifies the hexagonal weight lattice. The flavour-representations section constructs the flavor triplet and antitriplet from unknot configurations and assigns the charge quantum numbers (isospin I_3, hypercharge Y). The meson-octet section derives the meson octet via the tensor decomposition \mathbf{3} \otimes \bar{\mathbf{3}} = \mathbf{8} \oplus \mathbf{1}, realised through the \bowtie_K product. The baryon-multiplet section extends to baryons: \mathbf{3} \otimes \mathbf{3} \otimes \mathbf{3} = \mathbf{10} \oplus \mathbf{8} \oplus \mathbf{8} \oplus \mathbf{1}, with the symmetric channel yielding the decuplet and the Borromean baryon (Definition) providing the structural realisation. The colour-algebra section derives the color \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{c}} gauge algebra from octonionic stabilisation. The q-deformation section develops the q-deformation of the hexagonal weight lattice and connects it to the hyperbolic geometry of knot complements. The dictionary section consolidates the complete knot--particle--force dictionary. The open-problems section records the open problems.

Epistemic tiers. Each statement below is marked with one of four tiers, used in the same sense as in the Standard-Model appendix: proved (with a complete proof); derived (obtained from framework structure without fitted parameters); standard (a theorem of the ambient mathematics --- Coxeter theory, Schur--Weyl duality, \mathrm{SU}(3) representation theory --- cited, not re-derived here, and carrying no QOU content on its own); conditional (a rigorous consequence of a named hypothesis, principally N = 3); and open (a precisely identified missing object).

What this chapter does not do. It does not derive flavour \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}}. The eightfold-way classification is reproduced conditionally on N = 3, and N = 3 is not available: the framework supplies \dim V = 2. Most of the representation theory below is tier standard --- correct, and correctly applied, but true of any \mathrm{SU}(3) and not evidence for the framework. What the chapter contributes is the placement of the braid dictionary against that classification, one derived entry (I_3 on the nucleon doublet), and a sharpened statement of what is missing. The consolidated ledger is the open-problems section.
prop:a2-from-three-strands:
Proposition The A_2 root system from the Hecke algebra H_3(q). The Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_3(q) has Coxeter type A_2, and the associated weight lattice supplies the (I_3, Y) coordinates used throughout this chapter.

Scope. This is a statement about the A_2 of the Coxeter group W(A_2) \cong S_3 acting on the three strands, and it holds by construction: the braid group on n strands has Coxeter type A_{n-1}, so n = 3 puts A_2 here by definition. Nothing about the substrate is derived from it. In particular this is not the A_2 = \mathfrak{sl}_3 of flavour \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}}, which is the Schur--Weyl partner acting on the fibre V and requires \dim V = 3. Items 1--3 below are the standard braid/Coxeter dictionary, recorded for reference; item 4 and the weight-lattice paragraph are what the chapter actually uses.

Concretely:

  1. The generators T_1, T_2 of H_3(q) satisfy the braid relation T_1 T_2 T_1 = T_2 T_1 T_2 and the quadratic Hecke relation (T_i - q)(T_i + q^{-1}) = 0. The braid relation is the defining relation of the Coxeter group W(A_2) \cong S_3.

  2. The Cartan matrix of A_2 is

  a_{ij}
  = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ -1 & 2 \end{pmatrix}.

This is read off from the Coxeter presentation in the usual way: the braid relation T_1 T_2 T_1 = T_2 T_1 T_2 has length m_{12} = 3, and a_{ij} = -2\cos(\pi/m_{ij}) gives a_{12} = a_{21} = -1, with a_{ii} = 2 by normalisation. For |i - j| > 1 the generators commute (m_{ij} = 2) and a_{ij} = 0. A counting formula of the shape a_{ij} = 2\delta_{ij} - |\{T_iT_jT_i = T_jT_iT_j\}| would only re-encode the presentation; it is not an independent derivation of the Cartan data.

  1. The six roots of A_2 are the elements \{\pm\alpha_1, \pm\alpha_2, \pm(\alpha_1 + \alpha_2)\}, where \alpha_1, \alpha_2 are the simple roots associated to T_1, T_2. The angle between adjacent roots is \pi/3 (that is, 120° between a root and its negative), reflecting the Coxeter number h = 3 of A_2. The Weyl group W(A_2) \cong S_3 acts by permuting the three strands.

  2. At q = 1 (the classical limit), H_3(q) reduces to the group algebra \mathbb{C}[S_3], and the A_2 root system is the standard one. For q \neq 1 (the substrate-deformed case), the root system acquires a q-deformed inner product: the quantum Killing form \langle \alpha_i, \alpha_j \rangle_q = [a_{ij}]_q, where [n]_q = (q^n - q^{-n})/(q - q^{-1}) is the q-integer.

The hexagonal weight lattice of A_2 is the 2-dimensional lattice generated by the fundamental weights \omega_1, \omega_2 dual to the simple roots. Each irreducible representation of H_3(q) is labelled by a dominant integral weight (\lambda_1, \lambda_2) with \lambda_i \geq 0, and the weights of the representation sit at the vertices of a hexagonal pattern in the (I_3, Y) plane, where

  I_3 = \tfrac{1}{2}(\lambda_1 - \lambda_2),
  \qquad
  Y   = \tfrac{1}{3}(\lambda_1 + \lambda_2).

The fundamental representation \mathbf{3} has weights \{(1,0), (0,1), (-1,-1)\}, forming an equilateral triangle. The adjoint representation \mathbf{8} has weights forming a regular hexagon with multiplicity 2 at the origin.
rem:q-deformation-weight-lattice:
Remark The q-deformation and the invariance of the root datum. Two distinct occurrences of the integer 2 appear in the classical A_2 Serre relation and root system: one is a binomial coefficient that deforms into the Gaussian integer [2]_q = q + q^{-1} under Drinfeld–Jimbo quantization, whereas the other is the diagonal Cartan entry a_{ii} = 2 that remains constant for all q. Separating these two roles clarifies what the substrate parameter q_0 deforms in the eightfold-way classification and what remains rigid.

The two 2s. The classical Serre relation for A_2 reads

  e_i^2 e_j - 2\, e_i e_j e_i + e_j e_i^2 = 0,

where the coefficient 2 is the binomial coefficient \binom{2}{1} = \binom{1 - a_{ij}}{1}, with a_{ij} = -1 the off-diagonal Cartan entry. Meanwhile, the diagonal Cartan entry is a_{ii} = 2, which appears in the root angle formula \cos\theta = a_{ij}/a_{ii} = -1/2, giving \theta = 120°.

The Drinfeld--Jimbo quantization replaces the binomial 2 by the Gaussian binomial [2]_q = q + q^{-1}:

  e_i^2 e_j - [2]_q\, e_i e_j e_i + e_j e_i^2 = 0.

The Cartan entry a_{ii} = 2 is untouched. The angle \cos\theta = -1/2 does not become \cos\theta_q = -(q + q^{-1})/2. These are two different mathematical objects that coincide numerically at q = 1: one is a binomial coefficient, the other is a normalization constant.

What is q-independent — proved here. The following are proved:

  • The off-diagonal entry a_{12} = -1 and the Serre exponent 1 - a_{12} = 2.
  • The q-Serre coefficient [2]_q genuinely moves with q --- witnessed at q = 2, where the framed binomial is 5 and the framed Cartan diagonal is 4 --- while the Cartan datum does not. The conjunction of the two is the "two 2s" separation , and it is the conjunction, not either half alone, that carries the content: constancy of the Cartan datum is true by construction and is compatible with both sides being constant, which is exactly the confusion at issue.
  • For (q-1)^2 \neq 0 the two differ ; they agree at q = 1 .
  • The root-angle ratio \cos\theta = a_{ij}/a_{ii} = -1/2 .

What is not established here. That Drinfeld--Jimbo quantisation leaves the root datum invariant is a theorem of Lusztig/Kashiwara, cited here and not proved in this work; it belongs to the "standard, but not proved here" list below, not to the proved list above. What is proved is the arithmetic of the separation on the A_2 datum, which is a weaker statement and should not be cited for the stronger one.

What is q-independent — standard, but not proved here. These follow from the Drinfeld--Jimbo construction and are cited here, not proved:

  • The root lattice \Lambda_R = \mathbb{Z}\alpha_1 \oplus \mathbb{Z}\alpha_2 and the weight lattice \Lambda_W = \mathbb{Z}\omega_1 \oplus \mathbb{Z}\omega_2.
  • The Weyl group W(A_2) \cong S_3.
  • Weight multiplicities: for generic q the representation category \mathrm{Rep}\,\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{g}) is tensor-equivalent to \mathrm{Rep}\,\mathfrak{g}. Crystal bases exist precisely because the weight combinatorics is q-independent (the q \to 0 limit retains the same lattice).

What q does deform.

  • The braiding: the R-matrix of \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{sl}_3) depends on q and governs the braid group action on tensor products.
  • The quantum dimensions: \dim_q(V_\lambda) = \prod_{\alpha > 0} [\langle \lambda + \rho, \alpha^\vee \rangle]_q / [\langle \rho, \alpha^\vee \rangle]_q.
  • The Markov trace: \tau_q(\beta) on H_n(q) varies with q, producing q-dependent link invariants (Jones polynomial, HOMFLY-PT).
  • The crossing energy: \mathfrak{E}_\times(q) = \tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}), which governs mass splittings in the framework.

Consequence for the eightfold way. The hexagonal weight lattice of A_2 is rigid under q-deformation. The octet and decuplet patterns do not "bend" or become hyperbolic at q = q_0. What changes is the dynamics on the lattice: transition amplitudes, mass splittings, and mixing angles all depend on q_0 through the Hecke algebra representations, while the classification pattern itself --- which states go where on the hexagon --- is q-independent.

The classification thus holds for any q, while the quantitative predictions (mass ratios, decay rates) are specific to q = q_0.
rem:flavor-charge-assignments:
Remark Flavor charge assignments and the hypercharge gap. The A_2 weight lattice of the A_2 proposition assigns two quantum numbers to each state: the third component of isospin I_3 and the hypercharge Y, related to the fundamental weights by

  I_3 = \tfrac{1}{2}(\lambda_1 - \lambda_2),
  \qquad
  Y   = \tfrac{1}{3}(\lambda_1 + \lambda_2).

The electric charge is then the Gell-Mann--Nishijima relation Q = I_3 + Y/2.

Derived quantity: isospin I_3. The writhe-to-isospin map w \mapsto I_3 is derived in the framework without fitted parameters. Over the nucleon doublet, the proton braid \mathfrak{p} and neutron braid \mathfrak{n} carry writhes whose difference reproduces \Delta I_3 = 1 scale-free. This identifies I_3 as the writhe coordinate on the A_2 weight lattice. These writhes are those of the inter-nucleon arc, w(\mathfrak{p}) = +1 and w(\mathfrak{n}) = -1. The ruled nucleon word (\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}^{-1})^3 is the same for both nucleons and has writhe 0, so on the word itself the writhe does not separate them; there I_3 is the weight of the up and down strand labels.

Open quantity: hypercharge Y. The proton and neutron share Y = +1 while their writhes differ. This falsifies every injective map from the writhe to Y, in particular the linear map Y = c\,w that a framing phase q^{w c} would give. It does not falsify every function of the writhe: a non-injective one such as Y = w^2/4 passes the proton–neutron test. What does force a second invariant is the charge side. The quark charges are not a function of the writhe (the anti-up and down crossings share the writhe -1 but carry -\tfrac{2}{3} and -\tfrac{1}{3}; see the Coulomb-charge definition), and if both Q and I_3 were functions of the writhe then so would be Y = 2(Q - I_3). Since I_3 is read here as the writhe coordinate, a hypercharge independent of the writhe requires a charge Q that is not the halved writhe. The framework therefore requires a second invariant, independent of the writhe, to instantiate Y.

The candidate direction, recorded without endorsement, is the ribbon-framing twist. In the categorical braid representation, each strand carries a framing datum whose total T(t) is independent of the crossing word (hence independent of the writhe w). The candidate hypercharge is

  Y_t = 2\bigl(Q_{\mathrm{twist}} - I_3\bigr),
  \qquad
  Q_{\mathrm{twist}} = \frac{T(t)}{3},

where T(t)/3 is the colour-tube charge quantum of the quark picture (the helon-model normalisation of Sundance O. Bilson-Thompson [bilson-thompson2005]; in the braided-ribbon-graph formulation of Sundance O. Bilson-Thompson, Fotini Markopoulou, and Lee Smolin [bilsonthompson2007, §I, §V], strand twists define noiseless U(1)-charged subsystems conserved under local evolution moves, without claiming to derive the Standard Model interactions). The Gell-Mann--Nishijima relation holds by construction if and only if Q_{\mathrm{twist}} = Q against an independently derived electric charge Q --- a falsifiable consistency condition. The halved writhe of the Coulomb-charge definition cannot play that role, since it is not the electric charge, so the condition has no derived right-hand side yet.

Status and batteries. Neither the candidate nor any alternative has been wired. Any hypercharge proposal must pass two batteries before instantiating the class:

  1. Gell-Mann--Nishijima consistency: Q = I_3 + Y/2 must hold against an independently derived Q and I_3 on the nucleon doublet, without tuning a coupling. No derived Q exists yet, so this battery cannot currently be run against anything but the Standard-Model table.
  2. First-generation spectrum: The Y values of u, d, e^-, \nu_e must reproduce \{+1/3, +1/3, -1, -1\} (left-handed) and \{+4/3, -2/3, -2, 0\} (right-handed), satisfying the \mathbb{Z}_6 compatibility relations of John C. Baez and John Huerta [baez-huerta2010].

A candidate requiring a fitted scale to pass either battery is a fit, not a derivation, and does not instantiate this class.

Enumeration result, and why it carries no corroboration. The battery has been run over all 10{,}000 helon-style assignments (3 strands per fermion, per-strand twist in \{-1, 0, +1\}), of which 4 survive. That ratio must not be read as a 2500\!:\!1 filter: the battery collapses to a single linear equation per flavour, and the surviving count is multiset counting. The following are proved:

  1. The spectrum battery is exactly T = 3Q. Both the candidate Y_t = 2(Q_{\mathrm{twist}} - I_3) and the target Y = 2(Q - I_3) carry the same -2I_3, which cancels. What remains is Q_{\mathrm{twist}} = Q --- the defining equation of Q_{\mathrm{twist}}, not a test of it. The battery constrains nothing about isospin.
  2. The nucleon-doublet check is entailed, by charge additivity alone: T_{\mathfrak{p}} = 2T_u + T_d = 3(2Q_u + Q_d) follows from T = 3Q on the quarks, so no surviving assignment can fail it. As implemented it also states one condition twice --- its second clause 2(T_{\mathfrak{p}}/3 - 1/2) = 1 clears to T_{\mathfrak{p}} = 3, which is its own first clause.
  3. The \mathbb{Z}_6 condition is not a filter. As implemented it is a function of the Standard-Model table alone and never sees the candidate assignment; it runs as an input assertion and cannot exclude any multiset.

So each flavour is filtered independently by one equation, and 4 = 1 \times 2 \times 2 \times 1 counts the multisets of three twists from \{-1,0,+1\} with the required totals 3Q = (2, -1, 0, -3). The u-quark twist \{0,1,1\} and the electron twist \{-1,-1,-1\} are the two totals admitting a single multiset --- a fact about writing 2 and -3 as a sum of three elements of \{-1,0,+1\}, not about the framework; the d-quark and neutrino each admit two. Passing the battery is therefore equivalent to choosing t with \sum_i t_i = 3Q, which is always possible.

The open content is unchanged and is the whole question: whether the twist multisets are forced by the framework's braid words rather than only consistent with them.

A derived-twist repair, tested and refuted (scope-(a)). The defect above is that t is a free label. The natural repair is to replace it with the canonical twist of the ribbon category --- on a simple object the twist acts by a scalar whose exponent is the content sum c(\lambda) = \sum_{(i,j) \in \lambda} (j - i), a derived per-block integer. Taking Q = c(\lambda)/3 is parameter-free. It does not work: at n = 3 the content sums are \{3, 0, -3\}, giving the integer charges \{+1, 0, -1\} with no third-integer charge at all, and no n \le 8 yields both quark charges \{+2/3, -1/3\} . This is scope-(a) for the plain content-sum reading, not an exclusion of the ribbon route: other normalisations remain untested.

What the hypercharge must supply for a Coulomb term. On the nucleon doublet lepton number vanishes, so the Gell-Mann--Nishijima hypercharge equals the baryon number, Y = B = 1 for both proton and neutron. Per strand this is B = \tfrac{1}{3}, and the strand charge Q = T_3 + B/2 gives u \mapsto \tfrac{2}{3}, d \mapsto -\tfrac{1}{3} and a three-strand block with a up strands the charge a - 1. So on the baryon sector the content of Y is a derived reading of B; the non-strange identification Y = B with the Milnor triple linking number of the three colour tubes is a conjecture with no instance, and the lepton sector further needs a lepton number for Y = B - L.

Hypercharge alone does not give a Coulomb pair term. The exchange of the unbroken neutral bosons between two particles has charge factor g^2\,T_3T_3' + g'^2\,(Y/2)(Y'/2), with no T_3 \otimes Y cross term. On two three-quark blocks (Y = 1, T_3 = \pm\tfrac{1}{2}) it takes the same value on the proton pair and the neutron pair: it is an isospin coupling with no Coulomb part. It splits identically as

  g^2\,T_3T_3' + g'^2\,\tfrac{Y}{2}\tfrac{Y'}{2}
  = e^2\,QQ' + g_Z^2\,(T_3 - s^2 Q)(T_3' - s^2 Q'),

with e^2 = g^2g'^2/(g^2+g'^2), s^2 = g'^2/(g^2+g'^2) and g_Z^2 = g^2+g'^2. The first term is the Coulomb factor, zero whenever a neutron is involved. On nucleon blocks the exchange with a fraction \lambda of the second term kept has the Coulomb form if and only if \lambda = 0, and the remaining coefficient e^2 vanishes exactly when g'^2 = 0. Coulomb is therefore the unbroken W^3 + B exchange minus the Z exchange, and it needs, besides Y: the mixing s^2 = \sin^2\theta_W, and a Z mass scale that removes the second term at nuclear distance. Neither is derived in this framework: the electroweak torus-link triplet of the electroweak conjecture orders m_W < m_Z < m_H by crossing number but fixes no absolute scale.

Split-bundle framing F = V_2 \oplus W_3^* and conditional hypercharge coupling. In the Standard Model appendix, the missing hypercharge and the missing three-dimensional partner are shown to be one conditional gap rather than two independent knobs. If the two-dimensional fibre V_2 (z_2 = q^3/(q^2+1)) is paired with a three-dimensional partner W_3^* (z_3 = q^3/[3]_q = q^5/(q^4+q^2+1), separated from z_2 by the identity z_2 - z_3 = q^3 / ((q^2+1)(q^4+q^2+1)) \neq 0) inside F = V_2 \oplus W_3^*, then over any field of characteristic outside \{2, 3\} the traceless centralizer \mathrm{diag}(y_2, y_2, y_3, y_3, y_3) satisfies 2 y_2 + 3 y_3 = 0 if and only if y_3 = -\tfrac{2}{3} y_2. Fixing the doublet normalisation y_2 = 1 pins y_3 = -\tfrac{2}{3}, gives the exterior-pair quark doublet in V_2 \otimes W_3^* hypercharge y_2 + y_3 = +\tfrac{1}{3}, and yields the Killing traces \mathrm{tr}(T_3^2) = \tfrac{1}{2} and \mathrm{tr}((Y_F/2)^2) = \tfrac{5}{6}, hence the unrenormalized Weinberg ratio \mathrm{tr}(T_3^2)/(\mathrm{tr}(T_3^2) + \mathrm{tr}((Y_F/2)^2)) = \tfrac{3}{8}. On single strands, combining the weak-crossing sign s_2 \in \{\pm 1\} with the W_3 versus W_3^* triality orientation \tau_3 \in \{\pm 1\} via Q = \tfrac{1}{2} s_2 + \tfrac{1}{6} \tau_3 reproduces (+\tfrac{2}{3}, -\tfrac{1}{3}, +\tfrac{1}{3}, -\tfrac{2}{3}) on (u, d, \bar d, \bar u) and separates \bar u (-\tfrac{2}{3}) from d (-\tfrac{1}{3}) by +\tfrac{1}{3} \neq 0 despite their identical crossing sign -1. This implication is proved conditionally on W_3^*: constructing W_3 categorically in the multi-fibre groupoid remains the open antecedent.
prop:meson-octet-decomposition:
Proposition The meson octet via \mathbf{3} \otimes \bar{\mathbf{3}}. The tensor product of the fundamental triplet and its conjugate decomposes as \mathbf{3} \otimes \bar{\mathbf{3}} = \mathbf{8} \oplus \mathbf{1}, yielding the meson octet and the flavor singlet.

A meson is a quark--antiquark bound state. In the flavor \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}} classification, a quark transforms in the fundamental \mathbf{3} and an antiquark in the conjugate \bar{\mathbf{3}}. The tensor product decomposes into the adjoint (octet) and the trivial (singlet) representations:

  \mathbf{3} \otimes \bar{\mathbf{3}}
  = \mathbf{8} \oplus \mathbf{1}.
  \qquad (9 = 8 + 1)

The \mathbf{8} (adjoint representation) has weights forming a regular hexagon with double multiplicity at the origin, sitting in the (I_3, Y) plane. Weights are recorded in the quark-count coordinates (\lambda_1, \lambda_2) = (n_u - n_s,\; n_d - n_s) used for the \mathbf{3} in the A_2 proposition, so that the charge formulas I_3 = \tfrac{1}{2}(\lambda_1 - \lambda_2) and Y = \tfrac{1}{3}(\lambda_1 + \lambda_2) of that proposition apply verbatim to every row below:

Weight I_3 Y Meson identification
(1, -1) +1 0 \pi^+\ (u\bar{d})
(-1, 1) -1 0 \pi^-\ (d\bar{u})
(2, 1) +\tfrac{1}{2} +1 K^+\ (u\bar{s})
(1, 2) -\tfrac{1}{2} +1 K^0\ (d\bar{s})
(-2, -1) -\tfrac{1}{2} -1 K^-\ (s\bar{u})
(-1, -2) +\tfrac{1}{2} -1 \bar{K}^0\ (s\bar{d})
(0, 0)_a 0 0 \pi^0\ (u\bar{u} - d\bar{d})/\sqrt{2}
(0, 0)_b 0 0 \eta\ (u\bar{u} + d\bar{d} - 2s\bar{s})/\sqrt{6}

The \mathbf{1} (singlet) is the \eta':

  \eta' = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}(u\bar{u} + d\bar{d} + s\bar{s}).

QOU realization. In the knot-particle dictionary, each meson is a quark--antiquark pair joined by the \bowtie_K product. The splitting \mathbf{3} \otimes \bar{\mathbf{3}} = \mathbf{8} \oplus \mathbf{1} is the trace splitting of a rigid category. Let V be the fundamental of U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_3) at generic q and V^* its dual, with coevaluation c\colon \mathbf{1} \to V \otimes V^* and evaluation e\colon V \otimes V^* \to \mathbf{1} (using the pivotal structure). The composite e \circ c is multiplication by the quantum dimension d = [3]_q = q^2 + 1 + q^{-2}, which is nonzero for real q \neq 0. Then p = d^{-1}\, c \circ e is an idempotent on V \otimes V^*. Its image is the singlet, the image of c, and the complementary idempotent 1 - p projects onto the kernel of e, the octet. At q = 1 this is the splitting of a 3 \times 3 matrix into its trace part and its traceless part. The Hecke algebra H_3(q) does not enter here: it has no three-dimensional irreducible and no tensor product of modules, and it acts on V^{\otimes 3} by Schur--Weyl duality, which is the baryon side.

The idempotent algebra holds in any k-linear category: given c\colon U \to W and e\colon W \to U with e \circ c = d \cdot 1_U and d \neq 0, the maps p and 1 - p are complementary idempotents, p \circ c = c, e \circ p = e, and e \circ (1 - p) = 0. The octet is not proved irreducible here, and U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_3) is not constructed.

Conditional on N = 3. This decomposition requires the flavor fundamental to be three-dimensional (N = 3). The N = 3 question is the chapter's central open problem. The tensor decomposition itself is a theorem of \mathrm{SU}(3) representation theory; its applicability to QOU depends on resolving how the three-dimensional flavor space arises from the multi-fibre groupoid or octonionic stabilization.
rem:meson-mass-splitting:
Remark Meson mass splitting from q-deformed dynamics. The q-deformation lifts the mass degeneracy of the meson octet. The eight states share the same hexagonal weight pattern but their masses split through the quantum dimension and crossing-energy formulas of the Hecke algebra.

The meson octet decomposition (\mathbf{3} \otimes \bar{\mathbf{3}} = \mathbf{8} \oplus \mathbf{1}) determines which states exist. The mass splitting of these states is a separate, q-dependent phenomenon governed by the Markov trace and the crossing energy.

q-independent structure. The weight lattice and the state assignments (which meson sits at which (I_3, Y)) are q-independent (Remark). The hexagonal pattern itself --- \pi^\pm at (\pm 1, 0), K^\pm at (\pm 1/2, \pm 1), \pi^0 and \eta at the origin --- is determined entirely by the Cartan matrix A_2, which the Hecke relation encodes independently of q.

q-dependent dynamics. Within the hexagonal pattern, the physical masses are governed by three q-dependent ingredients:

  1. Quantum dimensions: \dim_q(V_\lambda) = \prod_{\alpha > 0} [\langle \lambda + \rho, \alpha^\vee \rangle]_q / [\langle \rho, \alpha^\vee \rangle]_q. At q = 1 these reduce to the classical dimensions (all integer); at q \neq 1 they split.
  2. Crossing energy: \mathfrak{E}_\times(q) = \tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}), the energy cost per crossing in the Hecke algebra. This governs the mass contribution from each braid crossing in the meson's knot representative.
  3. Markov trace weights: \tau_q(\beta) assigns a q-dependent amplitude to each braid \beta, producing the mass endomorphism via the Frobenius integral.

The Gell-Mann--Okubo mass formula. In standard \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}} flavour physics, the meson masses obey the Gell-Mann--Okubo relation

  4 m_K^2 = 3 m_\eta^2 + m_\pi^2.

Gell-Mann--Okubo cannot test this. The relation is not something the framework should derive, and its \approx 6\% experimental deviation is not comparable with the \approx 3.3\% figure from the q-deformation of the adjoint quantum dimension.

First-order \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}} breaking means the mass operator is a singlet plus an octet piece transforming like \lambda_8, so that

  m^2(I, Y) \;=\; a \;+\; b\,Y \;+\; c\left(I(I+1) - \tfrac{Y^2}{4}\right)

for some constants a, b, c. Evaluated on the pseudoscalar octet --- \pi at (I,Y) = (1,0), K at (\tfrac12, \pm 1), \eta at (0,0) --- the Gell-Mann--Okubo combination collapses identically:

  4m_K^2 - 3m_\eta^2 - m_\pi^2 \;=\; 0
  \qquad\text{for \emph{all} } a, b, c .

This is proved over any commutative ring, together with the sharper consequence that two arbitrarily different breaking patterns give the same value of the combination, namely zero. In particular b --- the entire hypercharge dependence, which is the whole content of a breaking mechanism --- cancels .

Two consequences. First, if the QOU crossing-energy splitting is first-order octet then it reproduces Gell-Mann--Okubo automatically and exactly, and doing so is not evidence for the framework: every first-order octet model reproduces it equally well [gellmann1962, okubo1962]. Second, the only testable content is the \approx 6.4\% deviation, which measures the failure of first-order breaking through second-order operators and \eta--\eta' singlet mixing.

Second-order quantum Casimir curvature versus singlet mixing. An unconstrained second-order polynomial in (I(I+1), Y) surjects onto every scalar residual over \mathbb{Q}, so a second-order fit carries no separating power unless the operator is fixed in advance. Replacing the classical isospin Casimir by the parameter-free rational quantum Casimir d_q(I, Y) = [I]_q[I+1]_q - [Y/2]_q^2 [kleinkreisler1996] (which evaluates over any field without square roots to d_q(1,0) = q + q^{-1}, d_q(0,0) = 0, and d_q(\tfrac{1}{2}, \pm 1) = (q + q^{-1})/(q + 2 + q^{-1})) yields an (a, b, c)-independent ratio for M(I, Y) = a + b\,Y + c\,d_q(I, Y) (c \neq 0):

  \frac{4 M_K - 3 M_\eta - M_\pi}{M_\pi - M_\eta}
  \;=\;
  -\left(\frac{q - 1}{q + 1}\right)^{\!2}
  \;=\;
  -\frac{(q - q^{-1})^2}{([2]_q + 2)^2}.

At q_0, this bar-even ratio equals -2.7168 \times 10^{-3}. Because m_\pi^2 - m_\eta^2 < 0 on the pseudoscalar octet whereas m_\Sigma - m_\Lambda > 0 on the baryon octet, the same negative factor predicts the observed sign on both octets simultaneously (4m_K^2 - 3m_\eta^2 - m_\pi^2 > 0 and 2(m_N + m_\Xi) - 3m_\Lambda - m_\Sigma < 0). In magnitude, however, single-q_0 isospin curvature accounts for only 1.21\% of the observed 6.43\% isospin-averaged meson deviation (normalized ratio -0.2247) and 0.82\% of the -0.57\% baryon deviation (normalized ratio -0.3330), confirming that \eta--\eta' singlet mixing and higher-order \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}} breaking dominate the empirical residual.

The \approx 3.3\% figure is not a competing prediction. It is the q-deformation of \dim_q of the adjoint, a dimension rather than a mass splitting, and not a quantity that can appear on either side of the relation. Comparing the two numbers was a category error, and the comparison is withdrawn.

Ordered 3-strand gluon clasp for neutral flavours. Two-strand torus closures T(2, n) have vanishing hyperbolic volume and cannot distinguish an ordered constituent pair (n_1, n_2) from its swap (n_2, n_1) under symmetric content maps. Mapping the ordered antiquark--quark generation pair (n_1, n_2) \in \{3, 5, 7\}^2 to the parameter-free 3-strand gluon-clasp braid \beta_{\mathrm{clasp}}(n_1, n_2) = \sigma_1^{n_1}\sigma_2^{-n_2}\sigma_1\sigma_2^{-1} \in B_3 gives \mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z}) monodromy determinant 1 and trace 2 n_1 n_2 + n_1 + n_2 + 3 \in \{27, 41, 55, 63, 85, 115\} > 2 (strictly pseudo-Anosov across all nine generation pairs, while the real-substrate S^{(2,1)} trace at q_0 stays inside (-0.760, -0.291) near its q = 1 value -1). Although the 2 \times 2 S^{(2,1)} trace is symmetric under n_1 \leftrightarrow n_2, both the rank-2 (z_2) and rank-3 (z_3) full H_3(q) Markov traces separate \bar D^0 \mapsto (5, 3) from K^0 \mapsto (3, 5) by exact closed-form multiples of q^2 - q^{-2} (+0.2125 at z_2 and +0.1442 at z_3 for q = q_0).

Conditional on N = 3 and on Y. Mass splittings between isospin multiplets (for example \pi against K) depend on the hypercharge Y, which is open (the flavour-representations section). Within an isospin multiplet (for example K^+ against K^0), the splitting is purely electromagnetic and arises from the writhe difference, which is derived.
rem:vector-meson-nonet: Remark The vector nonet: singlet–octet mixing is the content-bearing target. The pseudoscalar octet of the meson-octet proposition is one of two nonets with identical \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}} content. The other is the vector nonet 1^- --- \rho, K^*, \omega, \phi --- obtained from the same \mathbf{3} \otimes \bar{\mathbf{3}} = \mathbf{8} \oplus \mathbf{1} with the quark spins aligned rather than anti-aligned. The two nonets mix their octet and singlet almost oppositely, and no \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}}-symmetric statement distinguishes them. That makes the mixing the first eightfold-way quantity whose derivation would carry information.
prop:schur-weyl-eightfold:
Proposition Eightfold-way multiplets via quantum Schur--Weyl duality. The eightfold-way multiplets --- decuplet (\mathbf{10}), octet (\mathbf{8}), and singlet (\mathbf{1}) --- are the quantum Schur--Weyl partners of the Hecke algebra H_3(q) acting on V^{\otimes 3}.

Quantum Schur--Weyl duality (Jimbo [jimbo1986]) states that \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{gl}_N) and H_n(q) are mutual centralizers on V^{\otimes n}:

  V^{\otimes n}
  \cong \bigoplus_{\substack{\lambda \vdash n \\ \ell(\lambda) \leq N}}
    V_\lambda^{\mathfrak{gl}_N} \otimes S^\lambda_{H_n(q)},

where \lambda ranges over partitions of n with at most N rows, V_\lambda^{\mathfrak{gl}_N} is the irreducible \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{gl}_N)-module labelled by \lambda, and S^\lambda_{H_n(q)} is the irreducible Hecke module (Specht module) labelled by the same partition.

At n = 3 (three-strand braiding) and N = 3 (three-dimensional fundamental representation), the decomposition reads:

  V^{\otimes 3}
  \cong
  \underbrace{V_{(3)}}_{\dim = 10}
    \otimes S^{(3)}
  \;\oplus\;
  \underbrace{V_{(2,1)}}_{\dim = 8}
    \otimes S^{(2,1)}
  \;\oplus\;
  \underbrace{V_{(1,1,1)}}_{\dim = 1}
    \otimes S^{(1,1,1)}.

The dimensions and multiplicities are:

\lambda \vdash 3 \dim V_\lambda^{\mathfrak{gl}_3} \dim S^\lambda_{H_3} Name
(3) 10 (decuplet) 1 symmetric
(2,1) 8 (octet) 2 mixed
(1^3) 1 (singlet) 1 antisymmetric

The total is 10 \cdot 1 + 8 \cdot 2 + 1 \cdot 1 = 27 = 3^3, as required. The Hecke block dimensions (1, 2, 1) are the multiplicities of the flavour irreps, not the irreps themselves.

The N = 3 question. The single-fibre tower of the braiding and Bring's-surface chapters has \dim V = 2 (the standard single-fibre construction yields a quantum form of \mathrm{SU}(2); the Descartes condition \chi(\mathcal{A}) = -6 is compatible with but does not uniquely force N = 2 --- see the \chi-rank audit). The decomposition at N = 2 is:

  V^{\otimes 3}
  \cong V_{(3)} \otimes S^{(3)}
  \;\oplus\;
  V_{(2,1)} \otimes S^{(2,1)},
  \qquad
  4 \cdot 1 + 2 \cdot 2 = 8 = 2^3.

The antisymmetric partition (1^3) is absent (three rows exceed N = 2). No choice of q restores it: the row cap is \ell(\lambda) \leq \dim V, which the single-fibre construction fixes at 2, and the Drinfeld--Jimbo quantisation does not change dimensions.

The obstruction, and what is proved about it. The following are proved:

  • The alternating channel \dim V_{(1^3)} = \binom{N}{3} vanishes if and only if N < 3. This is the obstruction in one line.
  • If the symmetric channel has dimension 10 then N = 3. The implication runs from the decuplet dimension to the flavour dimension, in that direction.
  • A one-dimensional alternating channel likewise pins N = 3.
  • The channel arithmetic closes at both values (8 = 4 + 4 + 0 at N = 2; 27 = 10 + 16 + 1 at N = 3), so the N = 2 deficit sits precisely in the vanishing alternating channel and not in some unaccounted-for piece.

What is not established here. The same caveat applies here as to the q-deformation of the weight lattice above, and it is load-bearing in this one place because N = 3 is the chapter's central open problem. What is proved is the arithmetic of the row cap on the channel dimensions: \dim V_{(1^3)}^{\mathfrak{gl}_N} is taken to be \binom{N}{3} and the reasoning is about \binom{N}{3} alone, every step an elementary binomial identity, a finite check, or linear integer arithmetic. That the hook-content formula gives \dim V_{(1^3)} = \binom{N}{3}, and that the Schur--Weyl row cap is \ell(\lambda) \leq N, are standard and cited, not proved; in particular Worpitzky's identity is not proved here. So the tier is standard mathematics, with a proved arithmetic instance --- not proved in the sense the other proved rows of this chapter use.

The conclusion is nonetheless correct, because the two cited inputs are textbook. The eightfold-way classification is not "approximately available" at N = 2 --- it is structurally unavailable. This is a scope-(b) exclusion, and the invariant justifying it is the Schur--Weyl row cap.

The N = 2 half of the duality is proved. The Jimbo action of H_n(q) on V^{\otimes n} with \dim V = 2 is constructed, and the following are proved over an ordered field at generic q: the induced trace is the Markov trace with z = q^3/(q^2+1); the kernel of the action is exactly the trace radical, i.e. the blocks with three or more rows ; and the image has dimension the Catalan number. Surjectivity onto the \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2) commutant is not claimed, and no N \geq 3 action is constructed, so the N = 3 statement above remains cited.

The two pinning results above, from the decuplet and from the singlet, run from an observed channel dimension to N = 3; what the framework requires is N = 3 supplied by a construction. That is the affirmative half, and it remains open.

Therefore, realising the full eightfold way requires N = 3. Within QOU, this N = 3 cannot arise from a single fibre. The remaining construction directions are:

  1. Multi-fibre groupoid: inequivalent fibre objects whose interaction space is three-dimensional (T3b).
  2. Octonionic G_2 stabilizer: the Günaydin--Gürsey \mathbf{7} = \mathbf{1} \oplus \mathbf{3} \oplus \bar{\mathbf{3}} provides a non-self-dual triple from \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{c}} \subset G_2.

Status of the \mathrm{Sym}^2 gate. The gate is the requirement that \mathrm{Sym}^2(W) contain no singlet. Its representation-theoretic content is proved: at dimension three, passing the gate forces a complex-type summand, so the icosahedral triple T_1 --- a rotation representation of A_5 \subset \mathrm{SO}(3), hence real --- fails , while the octonionic \mathbf{3} is not excluded, on the decomposition \mathrm{Im}(\mathbb{O}) \cong \mathbb{R} \oplus \mathbb{C}^3 taken from the literature [gunaydin-gursey1973]. That the Günaydin--Gürsey triple is complex type is the cited input, not a proved one, so the octonionic route is not excluded rather than proved to pass. Whether the route yields flavour \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}} (not just colour \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{c}}) remains open.
prop:borromean-decuplet:
Proposition The baryon decuplet as symmetric Borromean channel. The baryon decuplet --- the 10-dimensional fully symmetric channel of the Schur--Weyl decomposition V^{\otimes 3} --- is realized by the Borromean baryon (Definition) with symmetric quark content.

The Schur--Weyl decomposition at N = 3, n = 3 assigns the partition \lambda = (3) to the fully symmetric subspace of V^{\otimes 3}, which has dimension \binom{N+n-1}{n} = \binom{5}{3} = 10. The 10 states correspond to the 10 elements of the weight diagram, a triangle with vertices at (3,0,0), (0,3,0), (0,0,3) in quark-count coordinates (n_u, n_d, n_s) --- that is, the corners \Delta^{++}\ (uuu), \Delta^{-}\ (ddd) and \Omega^{-}\ (sss). The remaining seven states fill the edges and the centre, with \Sigma^{*0}\ (uds) at the centre:

State Content I_3 Y
\Delta^{++} uuu +3/2 +1
\Delta^{+} uud +1/2 +1
\Delta^{0} udd -1/2 +1
\Delta^{-} ddd -3/2 +1
\Sigma^{*+} uus +1 0
\Sigma^{*0} uds 0 0
\Sigma^{*-} dds -1 0
\Xi^{*0} uss +1/2 -1
\Xi^{*-} dss -1/2 -1
\Omega^{-} sss 0 -2

Borromean realization. Each decuplet state is a Borromean baryon: three quark-unknots joined by the Borromean link \mathcal{B}_3. The symmetric partition \lambda = (3) corresponds to the Hecke symmetrizer e_{(3)} = \sum_{\sigma \in S_3} T_\sigma, which --- once normalized --- projects onto the subspace where all three strands are interchangeable. The normalization is not bookkeeping: e_{(3)} satisfies e_{(3)}^2 = c\, e_{(3)} with c = \sum_{\sigma \in S_3} q^{\ell(\sigma)}, equal to |S_3| = 6 in the classical limit, so e_{(3)} is idempotent only after division by c and the symmetric channel is identifiable with \mathrm{Sym}^3 only where c is invertible. In characteristic 2 or 3 it is not, and the identification fails.

What the Borromean topology does and does not supply. The Borromean link carries an S_3 symmetry permuting its three components, so it is a consistent carrier for the symmetric channel. It does not, however, select that channel: the octet (2,1) and the singlet (1^3) live on the same three strands and are equally available to the same link. Brunnian-ness --- that removing any one component frees the other two --- is a statement about sublink triviality, and no argument in this framework connects it to the Young-symmetriser decomposition of V^{\otimes 3}. The channel selection is carried entirely by the Hecke projector, not by the topology.

Missing ingredient: spin and colour. The physical decuplet is spin-3/2, and what forces the flavour-symmetric channel for it is the requirement that the total wavefunction be antisymmetric once three-colour degrees of freedom are included, as originally proposed via parastatistics by O. W. Greenberg [greenberg1964] and via explicit three-triplet \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{c}} symmetry by M. Y. Han and Y. Nambu [han-nambu1965]: with colour antisymmetric and spin symmetric, flavour must be symmetric. This chapter derives neither the spin factor nor the colour antisymmetry, so the identification \lambda = (3) \leftrightarrow decuplet is at present a matching of dimensions and weights, not a derivation of the spin--flavour--colour selection rule. This is recorded as an open item in the open-problems section.

Octet versus decuplet and quantum dimension balance. The mixed partition \lambda = (2,1) gives the 8-dimensional baryon octet (proton, neutron, \Sigma, \Lambda, \Xi). The antisymmetric partition \lambda = (1^3) gives the singlet. The distinction between octet and decuplet is entirely carried by the Hecke module: the S^{(3)} projector (one-dimensional) selects the decuplet, while the S^{(2,1)} projector (two-dimensional) selects the octet. Over any field and for every q \neq 0, the quantum dimensions \dim_q(\mathbf{10}) = (q^2 + q^{-2})[5]_q, \dim_q(\mathbf{8}) = [2]_q[4]_q, and \dim_q(\mathbf{1}) = 1 satisfy the identity

  (q^2 + q^{-2})[5]_q + 2\,[2]_q[4]_q + 1 \;=\; [3]_q^3,

normalizing the rank-3 Ocneanu weights w_\lambda(q, z_3) = \dim_q(V_\lambda)/[3]_q^3 at z_3 = q^3/[3]_q to w_{(3)} + 2\,w_{(2,1)} + w_{(1^3)} = 1 ($10.6690 + 2 \times 8.2641

  • 1 = 28.1973 = [3]_{q_0}^3atq_0$).

Conditional on N = 3. As with all eightfold-way content, this derivation is conditional on the flavor fundamental being three-dimensional (Proposition). Realised on degree-3 homogeneous polynomials, \dim_K \mathrm{Sym}^3(W_3^*) = \binom{5}{3} = 10 whereas \dim_K \mathrm{Sym}^3(V_2^*) = \binom{4}{3} = 4, so at N = 2 the symmetric partition (3) yields only a 4-dimensional spin-3/2 quadruplet, not a decuplet.
prop:delta-quartet-isospin-ladder:
Proposition The \Delta quartet as the symmetric channel at two flavours. Let K be a commutative semiring satisfying the strong rank condition (every field qualifies), let V = Ku \oplus Kd be free on two generators u, d, and let \mathrm{Sym}^3 V be the space of homogeneous forms of degree 3 in u, d over K. Then \dim_K \mathrm{Sym}^3 V = 4. Assign to a monomial u^{n_u} d^{n_d} the label 2I_3 = n_u - n_d. On the four monomials of degree 3 this label takes exactly the values 3, 1, -1, -3, it is odd at every monomial, and distinct monomials carry distinct labels.

The model term. The two variables are the two quark flavours of the single-fibre tower, u with I_3 = +\tfrac12 and d with I_3 = -\tfrac12, and \mathrm{Sym}^3 V is the fully symmetric channel, partition \lambda = (3), of the Schur--Weyl decomposition of V^{\otimes 3} at N = 2 (Proposition). Its four basis monomials are named the \Delta quartet:

State Monomial (n_u, n_d) 2I_3
\Delta^{++} u^3 (3, 0) +3
\Delta^{+} u^2 d (2, 1) +1
\Delta^{0} u d^2 (1, 2) -1
\Delta^{-} d^3 (0, 3) -3

The label is stated as the doubled value 2I_3 so that every statement stays in \mathbb{Z} and no division is performed.

Proof. The dimension is the stars-and-bars count: the degree-n forms in N variables are exactly the polynomials supported on the exponent vectors of total degree n, and these are in bijection with the multisets of size n drawn from N flavours, so \dim_K = \binom{N+n-1}{n}. At N = 2, n = 3 this is \binom{4}{3} = 4. For the labelling, every exponent vector of degree 3 satisfies n_u + n_d = 3, so 2I_3 = 3 - 2n_d with n_d \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}. This gives the four values 3, 1, -1, -3, each attained by u^{3-k} d^{k} for k = 0, 1, 2, 3. Each value is odd because n_u + n_d is odd. Two vectors with the same 2I_3 and the same total degree have the same n_u and the same n_d, so the label is injective. \square

What the labelling adds to the count. The dimension alone says only that the symmetric channel has four basis vectors. Attainment and closure fix the value set of 2I_3 as exactly \{3, 1, -1, -3\}, the weight set of isospin \tfrac32. Injectivity makes the four vectors four distinctly labelled states.

Scope. The statement concerns weights only. It constructs no action of the isospin group and no raising or lowering operators, and it makes no statement about spin, mass or any experimental quantity. It is not conditional on N = 3: unlike the decuplet (Proposition), whose corner \Omega^{-} requires a third flavour, the quartet lives entirely at N = 2. The oddness of 2I_3 depends on the degree: at even degree the same construction gives even values.
rem:decuplet-equal-spacing:
Remark The decuplet equal-spacing rule has no discriminating power. The eightfold way's signature triumph was Gell-Mann's 1962 prediction of the \Omega^-. Within the baryon decuplet the consecutive mass differences

  \mathfrak{m}(\Sigma^*) - \mathfrak{m}(\Delta), \qquad
  \mathfrak{m}(\Xi^*) - \mathfrak{m}(\Sigma^*), \qquad
  \mathfrak{m}(\Omega) - \mathfrak{m}(\Xi^*)

are observed to be nearly equal, so the mass of the then-undiscovered \Omega^- could be read off from the three lighter states. The particle was found in 1964 within 0.6\% of the extrapolated value.

The rule carries no information about the breaking mechanism. This is a theorem: the three spacings are all equal for every choice of the first-order octet-breaking parameters a, b, c, over any commutative ring. Their common value is -4b - 6c, and the second difference vanishes identically. Two arbitrarily different breaking patterns therefore give the same answer .
rem:u-spin-coleman-glashow:
Remark U-spin and the Coleman–Glashow relation: a third null result. Beyond isospin, the flavour \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}} contains two further \mathrm{SU}(2) subgroups: U-spin, exchanging d \leftrightarrow s, and V-spin, exchanging u \leftrightarrow s. U-spin is the useful one, because the electric charge is invariant under it --- d and s both carry Q = -\tfrac{1}{3} --- which makes the electromagnetic interaction a U-spin scalar.

The classical consequence is the Coleman--Glashow relation among the baryon octet's electromagnetic splittings,

  \bigl(\mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{p}} - \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{n}}\bigr)
  - \bigl(\mathfrak{m}_{\Sigma^+} - \mathfrak{m}_{\Sigma^-}\bigr)
  + \bigl(\mathfrak{m}_{\Xi^0} - \mathfrak{m}_{\Xi^-}\bigr)
  = 0,

which experiment satisfies to -0.064 MeV against splittings of 1.3 to 8.1 MeV --- about 0.8\% of the largest.

The relation carries no information about the breaking mechanism. This is a theorem: the combination vanishes for every choice of the six first-order parameters, over any commutative ring , so two arbitrarily different breaking patterns give the same answer.
prop:baryon-octet-decomposition:
Proposition The baryon octet and the degeneracy of its weight diagram. The mixed channel \lambda = (2,1) of V^{\otimes 3} carries the baryon octet. Unlike the decuplet, its weight diagram is degenerate --- and that degeneracy is the one piece of eightfold-way structure in this chapter which constrains rather than describes.

Conditional on N = 3 (Proposition), the three-fold product decomposes as

  \mathbf{3} \otimes \mathbf{3} \otimes \mathbf{3}
  \;=\;
  \mathbf{10} \oplus \mathbf{8} \oplus \mathbf{8} \oplus \mathbf{1},
  \qquad
  27 = 10 \cdot 1 + 8 \cdot 2 + 1 \cdot 1 .

The two octets are one flavour irrep counted with the multiplicity \dim S^{(2,1)} = 2 of its Hecke partner, not two different multiplets. The decuplet is treated in the preceding proposition; the octet is the subject here.
def:octonion-algebra:
Definition The octonion algebra \mathbb{O}. The octonion algebra \mathbb{O} is the 8-dimensional unital algebra with basis e_0, e_1, \dots, e_7, in which e_0 is the unit, each imaginary basis element squares to -1,

  e_i^2 = -1 \qquad (1 \le i \le 7),

and the imaginary units multiply by the cyclic rule

  e_i \, e_{i+1} = e_{i+3},
  \qquad
  e_{i+1} \, e_i = -e_{i+3},

with indices read modulo 7 on \{1, \dots, 7\}, extended to all of \mathbb{O} by bilinearity.

The algebra is alternative — every subalgebra generated by two elements is associative — but not associative: (e_1 e_2) e_4 = -e_1 (e_2 e_4). It carries the norm N(x) = \sum_i x_i^2, which is multiplicative, making \mathbb{O} a normed division algebra. Its automorphism group is the compact 14-dimensional exceptional Lie group G_2 = \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{O}), equivalently \mathrm{Der}(\mathbb{O}) \cong \mathfrak{g}_2 [baez2002].

Convention. The sign rule above is the Baez convention [baez2002], matching the multiplication fixed throughout this work. The choice is not canonical: 480 distinct multiplication tables are compatible with e_0 = 1 and e_i^2 = -1, all isomorphic as algebras but differing in which triples are quaternionic. Any statement that names a specific e_i e_j = \pm e_k is convention-dependent and must carry this qualification; statements about \mathbb{O} up to isomorphism, including \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{O}) = G_2, are not [albuquerque-majid1999].

Base ring. The product is realised over \mathbb{Q} in exact rational arithmetic. Nothing archimedean is required: the structure constants are integers, and the derivation count needs only \mathrm{char} \ne 2, 3.
prop:color-su3-from-g2:
Proposition Color \mathrm{SU}(3) from octonionic stabilization. The discrete color symmetry \mathrm{PSL}(2,7) arises from the octonionic automorphism group G_2 via the Fano plane, whose incidence structure encodes the octonion multiplication table. The octonion algebra is taken as an external input: it is not constructed from the categorical substrate, and the attempt to connect the two --- the bridge group S_4 \subset S_5 \cap \mathrm{PSL}(2,7) carrying local Fano data from the Bring surface to the Klein quartic --- is refuted below.

The S_4 bridge mechanism. The Bring surface \Sigma_4 (genus 4) has automorphism group S_5. The Klein quartic \Sigma_3 (genus 3) has automorphism group \mathrm{PSL}(2,7) of order 168 = 84(3-1), the Hurwitz bound. The group S_4 is the maximal common subgroup:

  1. S_4 \subset S_5 as the stabilizer of one letter (index 5).
  2. S_4 \cong \mathrm{Stab}(\mathrm{pt}) in \mathrm{PSL}(2,7) acting on the 7 Fano points (index 7).

The point stabilizer S_4 preserves the local Fano structure at the fixed point: the 3 lines through that point, encoding the 3 octonion multiplication triples involving the corresponding imaginary unit. Computationally verified :

  • S_4 acts transitively on the 3 lines through the fixed point,
  • S_4 acts transitively on the 4 lines not through the fixed point,
  • S_4 acts transitively on the 6 remaining Fano points,
  • the 3 local lines partition the 6 remaining points into 3 pairs.

Conjectured genus degeneration. The derivation chain from Bring to Fano is:

  \underbrace{\Sigma_4}_{g=4,\; S_5}
  \;\xrightarrow{\text{pinch}}\;
  \underbrace{\Sigma_3^{\mathrm{nod}}}_{g_{\mathrm{arith}}=4,\; S_4}
  \;\xrightarrow{\text{normalize}}\;
  \underbrace{\Sigma_3}_{g=3,\; \mathrm{PSL}(2,7)}

Pinching an S_4-invariant 1-cycle on \Sigma_4 produces a nodal curve of arithmetic genus 4 but geometric genus 3. The S_4 symmetry survives the pinch (it fixes the vanishing cycle). On the normalization \Sigma_3 of genus 3, the Hurwitz bound gives |\mathrm{Aut}| \leq 84(3-1) = 168, which \mathrm{PSL}(2,7) attains.

The gap in this argument. The Hurwitz bound is an upper bound; it does not force the automorphism group to be \mathrm{PSL}(2,7), and the generic genus-3 curve has small or trivial automorphism group. That S_4 embeds in \mathrm{PSL}(2,7) as a point stabilizer shows the enhancement is available, not that it occurs: nothing here rules out the normalization being a genus-3 curve whose automorphism group is exactly S_4, or any other group containing S_4. Maximality of the enhancement does not select it.

The S_4 bridge cannot select the Klein quartic. A stronger negative than the Hurwitz error: the S_4 datum has no separating power at all. The Fermat quartic x^4 + y^4 + z^4 = 0 is a genus-3 curve whose automorphism group (\mathbb{Z}/4)^2 \rtimes S_3 of order 96 also contains S_4 --- exhibited as V_4 \rtimes S_3 and verified by exact computation in \mathbb{Z}[i] arithmetic (element-order profile \{1{:}1,\, 2{:}9,\, 3{:}8,\, 4{:}6\}, V_4 normal, S_3 inducing the full symmetric action on V_4 \setminus \{1\}). So even a fully correct argument that the normalization has genus 3 and inherits S_4 stops short of the Klein quartic, because at least one other genus-3 curve satisfies both conditions.

The competitor set is in fact infinite. Fermat is not an isolated coincidence. The S_4-invariant ternary quartics form a two-dimensional space, so the genus-3 curves admitting S_4 contain an entire pencil

C_t : x^4 + y^4 + z^4 + t\,(x^2 y^2 + y^2 z^2 + z^2 x^2) = 0 ,

with parameter t (not \lambda, which throughout this chapter denotes a partition), smooth --- hence of genus 3 --- for every t outside \{2,\, -2,\, -1\}, with Fermat the single member t = 0. The fibres of t \mapsto [C_t] in moduli are finite, so infinitely many pairwise non-isomorphic genus-3 curves carry a faithful S_4 action. All of this is machine-verified in exact rational arithmetic, and only finiteness of the automorphism group is used --- the sharp Hurwitz bound is deliberately avoided here, for the reason given above. The S_4 bridge therefore fails not only to choose between two candidates, but to cut a \mathbb{P}^1 down at all.

Identifying the normalization therefore cannot be reduced to telling Klein and Fermat apart. Many invariants do that --- the automorphism-group order alone separates them, 168 against 96 --- while saying nothing about the rest of the family, and nothing whatever about which member the pinch produces. What is required is an invariant that the degeneration itself determines: read off the pinched cycle and the nodal curve, rather than computed from a shortlist of candidate targets. The decisive version is the period matrix. None has been computed. This is a scope-(a) negative: the degeneration itself is not refuted, only the argument offered for it.

The marked points obstruct the degeneration. There is extra data the pinch does supply, and it settles the question --- against the conjecture. Pinching a single non-separating cycle on a genus-4 curve yields a one-node curve of arithmetic genus 4 whose normalization has genus 3 together with two marked points --- the two preimages of the node, consistent with 3 + 1 = 4. Since the pinched cycle is S_4-invariant, S_4 preserves that pair setwise, so the object the degeneration produces is a pair (\Sigma_3, \{p, q\}) with an S_4-stable point pair, not a bare genus-3 curve.

No smooth plane quartic admits such a pair. Let \{p, q\} be S_4-stable; permuting it gives a homomorphism S_4 \to S_2 whose kernel has index 1 or 2, hence is S_4 itself or the unique index-2 subgroup A_4. Either way the line through p is an invariant 1-dimensional subspace of \mathbb{C}^3. But the 3-dimensional representation of S_4 is absolutely irreducible, and so is its restriction to A_4 --- each verified two independent ways, by commutant dimension and by character norm . An absolutely irreducible representation has no invariant line over any extension field, so no such pair exists: S_4 has no orbit of size \le 2 on \mathbb{P}^2 at all.

Consequently, under the three premises this chain itself asserts --- one S_4-invariant non-separating cycle (which is what arithmetic genus 4 and geometric genus 3 mean), S_4 acting faithfully on the normalization (which is what "S_4 survives" means), and a non-hyperelliptic normalization (which the Klein quartic is) --- the required configuration does not exist. This is a scope-(b) structural exclusion, licensed by a proved invariant rather than by a numerical near-miss, and unlike the two earlier failures it bears on the conjecture rather than on an argument for it.

What remains are the escapes, named precisely. A hyperelliptic genus-3 normalization is not excluded: its canonical map is 2-to-1 onto a conic, so its automorphisms do not act through \mathrm{PGL}_3 in the manner above, and such curves admitting S_4 do exist. The Klein quartic is not hyperelliptic, so that escape does not recover it. Nor is a pinch with several nodes or of a separating cycle excluded --- but either is a different claim from the one made here. What the argument does not touch at all is the Bring surface: it constrains the target, not the source.

Status: the S_4 bridge mechanism is computationally verified --- that is, S_4 does act on the local Fano data as claimed. The genus degeneration step is a different matter, and it is no longer unproved but excluded: as shown above, under its own three premises it is excluded. A pinch of the kind described cannot deliver a non-hyperelliptic genus-3 normalization, and the Klein quartic is non-hyperelliptic. Rescuing the colour route therefore requires giving up one of the three premises explicitly --- a hyperelliptic target, a multi-node or separating pinch, or a non-faithful S_4 --- and saying which.

\mathrm{PSL}(2,7) representation theory. Computationally verified: the group \mathrm{PSL}(2,7) \cong \mathrm{GL}(3, \mathbb{F}_2) has 6 conjugacy classes and 6 irreducible representations of dimensions

\begin{equation}\label{eq:psl27-irreps}
  \{1, 3, \bar{3}, 6, 7, 8\},
  \qquad
  \sum d_i^2 = 1 + 9 + 9 + 36 + 49 + 64 = 168 = |\mathrm{PSL}(2,7)|.
\end{equation}

The physical interpretation:

\dim Representation Physical role
1 trivial singlet
3 fundamental color triplet (q)
\bar{3} conjugate color antitriplet (\bar{q})
6 \mathrm{Sym}^2(\mathbf{3}) no singlet \Rightarrow complex type
7 natural on \mathrm{Im}(\mathbb{O}) imaginary octonions
8 adjoint of \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{c}} gluon octet

The 3 and \bar{3} are complex conjugate (not self-dual), matching the Günaydin--Gürsey decomposition \mathrm{Im}(\mathbb{O}) \cong \mathbb{R} \oplus \mathbb{C}^3 under \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{c}} \subset G_2 [gunaydin-gursey1973]. Non-self-duality is what the \mathrm{Sym}^2 gate consumes, so this is a load-bearing citation rather than an attribution: a self-dual 3 would carry a singlet in \mathrm{Sym}^2 and fail the gate.

Prior-art positioning. Deriving three-colour \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{c}} — introduced to resolve baryon antisymmetry by O. W. Greenberg [greenberg1964] and by M. Y. Han and Y. Nambu [han-nambu1965] — as the subgroup of G_2 = \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{O}) stabilizing a chosen imaginary octonion unit originates with Murat Günaydin and Feza Gürsey [gunaydin-gursey1973]. Subsequent algebraic Standard Model constructions embed colour alongside electroweak symmetries inside division-algebra tensor products \mathbb{R}\otimes\mathbb{C}\otimes\mathbb{H}\otimes\mathbb{O} (Geoffrey M. Dixon [dixon1994]; Cohl Furey [furey2016, furey2018]) or inside the automorphism and structure groups of the exceptional Jordan algebra J_3(\mathbb{O}) (Ivan Todorov and Michel Dubois-Violette [todorov2018, dubois-violette-todorov2018]; Latham Boyle [boyle2020]). In the present paper, \mathbb{O} is likewise an external algebraic input: the single-fibre \mathrm{SU}_q(2) substrate does not construct \mathbb{O}, and the S_4 genus-degeneration route from Bring's curve to the Klein quartic is excluded above.
